title: Inference Metrics — TTFT, TPOT, ITL, Goodput, P99

questions.question: Which components dominate TTFT (time to first token)?
options: Queue time, network request time, and prefill time
questions.explanation: The lesson defines TTFT = queue_time + network_request + prefill_time, so all three of those components, not decode time, dominate it.

questions.question: Which metric does the lesson call the one that actually matters for product?
options: Aggregate throughput in tokens per second
Goodput — fraction of requests meeting every SLO constraint simultaneously
questions.explanation: The lesson is explicit that throughput is a fleet-efficiency metric, but goodput -- the fraction of requests meeting every SLO constraint (TTFT, TPOT, and E2E) simultaneously -- is the one that reflects whether the product actually worked for users.

questions.question: Why is mean the wrong statistic to report for LLM latency?
options: Mean is never computable on streaming responses
Mean only works for prefill, not decode
LLM latency distributions are right-skewed; users routinely hit P99 outliers that mean hides
Mean is not supported by GenAI-Perf
questions.explanation: The lesson's example shows mean TPOT of 9 ms hiding a P99 TPOT of 65 ms, because a right-skewed distribution (a few requests sharing a batch with a long-prefill neighbor) means users regularly hit the tail that the mean averages away.

questions.question: Why do GenAI-Perf and LLMPerf disagree on TPOT for the same run?
options: GenAI-Perf excludes TTFT from the ITL calculation; LLMPerf includes it, so tool choice changes the number
LLMPerf uses microseconds and GenAI-Perf uses milliseconds
questions.explanation: The lesson's worked example shows GenAI-Perf starting ITL from token 2 (excluding TTFT) while LLMPerf starts from token 1 (including TTFT), producing different numbers (7.07 ms vs 12.00 ms) for the identical run.

questions.question: For long-output requests (>500 tokens), which metric dominates end-to-end latency?
questions.explanation: E2E = TTFT + TPOT * output_tokens + network_response, and the lesson states that for long outputs (>500 tokens) E2E is TPOT-dominated -- TPOT times output length outweighs the fixed TTFT and network terms.

questions.question: Which set best captures the lesson's reasonable consumer-facing SLO for a 70B chat model in 2026?
options: TTFT P99 800 ms, TPOT P99 25 ms, E2E P99 3 s for <300-token outputs, goodput >= 99%
Mean TTFT 10 ms, mean TPOT 1 ms
questions.explanation: The lesson gives exactly this SLO as the reasonable 2026 consumer-facing target: TTFT P99 <= 800 ms, TPOT P99 <= 25 ms, E2E P99 <= 3 s for <300-token outputs, and a goodput target >= 99%.
